We are seeking an experienced Associate Director, Head of Operational Excellence (OE) to join our Liverpool Site Leadership Team and play a pivotal role in shaping the future performance of one of CSL Seqirus' most important manufacturing sites. You will lead the site's Operational Excellence function and drive a culture of continuous improvement through the deployment of Lean, Six Sigma and the CSL Operating System (COS) to translate strategy into actionable operational priorities and financial benefits.  The role owns the operating model for the site management system, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement, ensuring COS is embedded as a durable management system rather than a discrete set of tools. It helps develop and implement scalable, standardized approaches that drive sustained improvements in operational effectiveness, quality, productivity, and cost performance at the site. Acting as a trusted advisor to the Site Leadership Team, you will coach and develop leaders in OE principles and influence decision-making through data-driven insights, structured problem solving and change leadership.

Reporting to the Manufacturing Site Lead, you will partner closely with senior leaders to identify performance opportunities, prioritise improvement initiatives and ensure sustainable business impact. Specifically, you will also:
• Develop and execute the site's Operational Excellence roadmap aligned to business strategy.
• Drive organisational focus on the critical metrics and outcomes that matter most.
• Build and grow a culture of continuous improvement by upskilling and creating a lean culture at all levels of the Liverpool organisation.
• Own the deployment of COS at site level through partnering with site leadership including agreeing improvement plans and managing the maturity assessment process.
• Facilitate Lean events, value stream improvements and structured problem-solving activities.
• Ensure robust governance, benefits tracking and sustainable implementation of improvements.
• Establish meaningful KPI frameworks and performance reporting.
• Analyse operational data to identify trends, risks and improvement opportunities.
• Drive root cause analysis and corrective actions to address systemic issues.
• Lead the successful adoption of strategic change initiatives across the site and strengthen the understanding of how change impacts day-to-day operations for all employees.
• Lead the annual Site Strategic Planning process.
• Working with leaders locally and colleagues globally, you will foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation and continuous learning.
• Lead, develop and engage the Operational Excellence team to build capability and deliver business outcomes
About You
To be successful, you will bring:
• Degree qualification in Engineering, Science, Business or a related discipline.
• Advanced qualifications (MBA, MSc or equivalent) highly regarded.
• Lean Six Sigma Black Belt preferred: Green Belt desirable.
• Credible Lean and Six Sigma subject matter expertise.
• Formal project management training, ideally with certification.
• 6+ years’ experience leading Operational Excellence, Continuous Improvement or Business Transformation initiatives and delivering measurable business outcomes within complex operational environments.
• Experience within pharmaceutical, biotechnology or highly regulated manufacturing environments.
• Effective leadership capability with experience leading and developing teams.
• Excellent stakeholder engagement, influencing and communication skills.
• Advanced analytical, problem-solving and process improvement expertise.
• Superb written and verbal communication skills and ability to drive results in cross-functional teams.
• Extensive experience in successfully leading and facilitating workshops.
• Experienced Change Practitioner.
• Senior team leadership experience.
Apply now if you're an experienced Operational Excellence leader ready to shape strategy, drive performance and build a culture of continuous improvement in an organisation making a meaningful difference to patients and communities worldwide.

About Waythrough
Waythrough provides specialist support across mental health, alcohol, drugs and related areas. We delivery high-quality, evidence-based services designed around the real needs of the people we serve.
Every year, we support around 125,000 people through over 250 services - and it's all made possible by our 3,500 brilliant staff and volunteers.
Make a real difference in your community
Are you passionate about helping others live safer, healthier, more independent lives? Join our team at Waythrough and support people facing challenges around mental health, substance use, housing or domestic abuse. This is more than just a job – it’s a chance to build meaningful relationships and create lasting change.
Together Drug and Alcohol Service is the commissioned community drug and alcohol provision for Devon. It provides a range of support, interventions and treatments for those wanting to make positive changes to their drug and/or alcohol use, as well as supporting family members and running campaigns and events that raise awareness of addiction and celebrate recovery in the community.
SMART Recovery is a four-point mutual aid programme focussing on any form of addictive behaviour. It focusses on building and maintaining motivation; managing thoughts, feelings, and emotions; coping with urges; and building a balanced lifestyle. SMART focusses on future recovery success rather than past experiences. All facilitators are trained through SMART Recovery UK.
Waythrough, as the overarching organisation that Together Drug and Alcohol Services sits within, holds licences to deliver SMART meetings across the South West Region in Devon and Dorset.
Details of the role & tasks
The Role:
Volunteers in this role will be facilitating or co-facilitating regular SMART meetings. Volunteer SMART facilitators will help to make newcomers feels welcome, and empower everyone in the meeting to contribute, should they wish to.
If not already trained, volunteers will need to complete the full SMART Recovery UK facilitator training programme. This role is ideally suited to people with lived experience of recovery, either directly, or through supporting a close friend or family member, although we welcome applications from anyone with an empathetic, non-judgemental attitude that can build strong working relationships with others.
Tasks may include:
• Sharing a group agreement at the start of each session, including the importance of respect and confidentiality.
• Facilitating meetings according to the SMART Recovery Meeting Structure – including a check-in, agenda setting, and check-out.
• Reporting any concerns, including related to safeguarding, that may arise in the group.
• Link closely with the group lead to plan and evaluate sessions.
• Procuring necessary resources such as flip chart, paper and pens, and setting up before/packing away after each meeting.
• Support the group lead with any admin tasks linked to the running of the SMART group. E.g. Completing SMART audits or liaising with Regional SMART Community Coordinator.
Personal qualities
Skills we would love you to bring to the role:
• Welcoming, friendly and an ability to put other people at ease
• Confident and calm in group settings
• Good IT skills – the SMART Recovery UK training all takes place electronically and includes submitting some written responses via email
• Non-judgmental towards people facing challenges in their lives, including around drug and/or alcohol use and/or mental health
• Good time keeping
• Able to work as part of a team, on own initiative and to instruction
• An understanding of Waythrough – information is available on our website
• A genuine interest in being part of the mission and vision of Waythrough
• Ability to maintain professional boundaries, adhere to Waythrough policies and media guidelines, engage in supervision, and complete relevant training
What We Offer

•
Discounts from various schemes

Training and personal development

A chance to make a real difference in people’s lives

Free induction and role-specific training

Job Type:

Build a brilliant future with Hiscox
The team and role
The UK Pricing team are a fundamental part of the Hiscox UK business, driving analytics and business insight that informs the direction of portfolio underwriting decisions. The UK Pricing team sits within the wider Portfolio Underwriting and Pricing function, whose primary objective is to provide pricing and underwriting services across the UK retail business, with the aim of providing market-leading risk selection and driving profitable growth across the portfolio.
The team reports directly to the UK Chief Underwriting Officer and collaborates closely with Underwriting, Distribution, Operations, Marketing, Reserving and Finance. The pricing team is split into Technical and Product-Facing analysts. Product-Facing Pricing Analysts focus more on monitoring, implementing and maintaining production prices, and work with senior stakeholders to prioritise pricing activity aligned with the UK strategy.
This role sits within the technical pricing area of the team. You will be someone who loves technical detail but can bring commercial understanding to provide insights that directly influence business decisions. Day to day, you will focus on creating, maintaining, monitoring and embedding pricing models. You will have a passion for data science and for seeing business outcomes influenced by your expertise.
As a Senior Pricing Analyst, you will drive pricing analysis and influence the growing book of non-standard high-net-worth household, motor, SME commercial and specialty lines. The Senior Pricing Analyst plays a critical role in supporting and influencing UK pricing and profitable growth.
Please note that this role does not require you to pursue, or to have previously pursued, actuarial qualifications.
What you'll be doing
• Design and manipulate underlying data models to produce standardised data tables that form the basis of all underlying technical pricing models.
• Act as the end-to-end architect of technical pricing models. Create models to predict claims frequency, claims severity, conversion, cancellation rates and other customer behaviours using GLMs and machine-learning techniques.
• Own a regular reporting cycle that enables the team to compare modelled predicted behaviours with actual observed behaviours, and decide when the cycle should trigger a revision or update to the underlying models.
• Take accountability for the infrastructure that enables the business to access technical pricing model insights, ensuring these insights are used to drive real change aligned with the UK strategy.
• Define and establish regular feedback cycles with Heads of Underwriting to support continuous improvement and refinement of technical pricing models, enhancing the ability to select and accurately price business according to the risk presented.
• Design, develop and produce regular reporting for the CUO and Heads of Underwriting to monitor the performance of the UK portfolio using technical pricing model outputs.
• Take accountability for your own pricing recommendations and for the performance of all pricing models used for your products.
• Act as a key point of contact for Underwriting Managers and Heads of Underwriting. Engage with them to understand underwriting strategy and identify how technical pricing can support their objectives. You will need to juggle conflicting priorities between senior stakeholders, build strong relationships, and influence and manage expectations.
• Work with and support the design and implementation of new technologies, including cloud-based data warehouses, data-visualisation products and new pricing software.
• Offer support and coaching to less experienced team members, sharing your experience and expertise to support their development.
Person specification
We are looking for an individual who is highly analytical, driven and detail-oriented, with a passion for excellent execution. You will need to be articulate and demonstrate a track record of good decision-making, working under pressure and to tight deadlines, with the ability to understand problems quickly and create and implement solutions.
Pricing experience is required for this senior analyst role. More importantly, you will have an excellent understanding of the nuances involved in performing detailed analytics, combined with a strong commercial mindset.
Our must-haves
• Graduate calibre, with at least three years of experience and proven success in a similar role.
• Practical application of in-depth statistical skills within a business environment.
• Strong analytical and pragmatic reasoning skills, with an aptitude for innovative problem-solving.
• High confidence in using data-analysis tools such as Excel and SQL.
• Knowledge of programming and statistical tools such as Python, Emblem and SAS.
• Experience of the end-to-end process of building technical pricing models.
• A high level of numerical competence and excellent data-gathering and manipulation skills.
• Experience of working closely with stakeholders and the ability to build strong working relationships.
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex information to technical and non-technical audiences.
• Deadline-oriented, hardworking, curious, passionate, enthusiastic and a self-starter.
Our nice-to-haves
• A good understanding of Commercial Lines and/or Personal Lines insurance through various distribution channels.
• Working towards or having attained relevant professional qualifications.

At Hiscox, we care about our people. We hire the best people for the job and are committed to diversity and creating a truly inclusive culture, which we believe drives success. Lloyd’s is the world’s leading insurance and reinsurance marketplace, bringing together the world’s leading risk takers to advance global progress.
Our strategy is focused on delivering strong underwriting performance, operating an efficient and flexible marketplace, and maximising the capital advantage of the Lloyd’s market — while continuing to build a Lloyd’s we are proud of.
How we deliver this, matters. We take the risk, make things happen, and own the outcome — working together across our global network to turn insight into impact.
Lloyd’s is recruiting for a Transformation Management Office Lead to help shape how change happens across Lloyd’s. This is an enterprise leadership role with real influence. You’ll give our senior leaders a clear view of our change portfolio, helping us make better decisions about where we invest, what we prioritise and how we turn ambition into sustained value. You won’t own every programme or business outcome. Instead, you’ll create the environment in which great delivery can happen: bringing clarity, evidence, constructive challenge and confidence to some of our most important decisions.
What you’ll do
You’ll lead and develop our Transformation Management Office across portfolio planning, governance and assurance, delivery excellence and value realisation.
You’ll:
• Create a clear, trusted enterprise view of change, covering investment, capacity, dependencies, delivery health, outcomes and value.
• Shape and prioritise our portfolio, helping senior leaders make informed investment, sequencing and capacity decisions.
• Lead our Change Delivery Framework, improving governance, decision rights and controls while keeping them proportionate and practical.
• Provide independent assurance, identifying risks early and helping leaders take timely corrective action.
• Set clear delivery standards, methods, tools and data expectations, while building capability across our change community.
• Strengthen how we define, measure and realise value, from the initial case for change through to post-implementation review.
• Turn complex portfolio information into concise, forward-looking insight for executive and governance forums.
• Build an inclusive, high-performing TMO that’s trusted by sponsors, business owners, programme leaders and delivery teams.
What you’ll bring
You’ll be an accomplished transformation or portfolio leader who can see the bigger picture without losing sight of what makes change succeed.
• Significant experience leading an enterprise PMO, EPMO, TMO, portfolio function or comparable transformation capability.
• Strong experience shaping and governing complex portfolios of business and technology change.
• The confidence and judgement to advise senior executives, facilitate difficult decisions and challenge constructively.
• A strong understanding of portfolio management, governance, assurance, risk and controls.
• Experience improving delivery frameworks, standards, reporting and governance.
• A track record of connecting investment and delivery to measurable outcomes and value.
• Strong analytical and commercial judgement, with the ability to turn complexity into clear choices.
• Leadership experience that shows you can build capability, create clarity and help diverse teams perform at their best.
• Experience in financial services, insurance, reinsurance or another complex regulated environment would be valuable, but we’re also interested in the perspective you can bring from elsewhere.
• Relevant portfolio, programme, project or change qualifications such as MoP, MSP, P3O, PRINCE2, APM, PMI or Prosci are welcome, but they’re not the only way to demonstrate your expertise.
Being inclusive at Lloyd’s is integral to how we work — and how we deliver impact.
We aim to build a diverse, inclusive environment that reflects the global markets we serve, where everyone is treated with dignity and respect and supported to reach their full potential.
We take the risk by challenging traditional thinking and being proactive about inclusion. That means being open and positive about workplace adjustments, prioritising health and wellbeing, and investing in diversity and inclusion training so everyone feels able to contribute and succeed.
We make things happen by turning our commitment into action. Through employee networks, mentoring, volunteering opportunities and sustained investment in professional development, we create an environment where inclusion is experienced day‑to‑day — not just talked about.
We own the outcome by focusing on impact. By bringing together diverse perspectives and the best minds in the industry, we work collaboratively with underwriters and brokers to create innovative, responsive solutions that share risk and solve complex problems across global markets.

Join us on our exciting journey! IQVIA™ is The Human Data Science Company™, focused on using data and science to help healthcare clients find better solutions for their patients. IQVIA offers a broad range of solutions that harness advances in healthcare information, technology, analytics and human ingenuity to drive healthcare forward.
ABOUT TEAM
The Evidence Synthesis practice is part of the IQVIA Real World Solutions (RWS). RWS brings together IQVIA initiatives that connect healthcare stakeholders through real-world evidence to demonstrate the value of medicines, enhance quality and drive improved outcomes.
ABOUT ROLE
Our industry-leading team is growing and seeking an experienced and enthusiastic technical specialist to support our Evidence Synthesis practice and Centre of Excellence (CoE). The role involves a blend of technical leadership, strategic problem-solving for complex research tasks, coding/programming, enhancing existing and developing new capabilities as senior member of our CoE, generation of business opportunities, as well as coaching and training of junior team members. As technical lead, the role requires strong hands-on expertise across areas of evidence synthesis such as feasibility assessments, direct and indirect treatment comparisons, population-adjustment (MAIC, STC, ML-NMR), surrogate endpoint evaluation, structured expert elicitation, survival analyses, external comparator arms etc. Besides working in integrated teams across geographies and functions, a key part of the role is to build and maintain effective client relationships to add value in a rapidly evolving environment.
REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE
In-depth expertise and hands-on experience with advanced evidence synthesis methods is essential. The role requires a good understanding of the health care sector and the pharmaceutical market, as well as general consulting methodologies and business practices. Experience in the delivery of consulting engagements is desirable.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Client engagements
•
Lead day-to-day activities of multiple evidence synthesis projects with the support of junior team members, including the development of statistical analysis protocols (SAP) and conduct of feasibility assessments, evidence synthesis by means of meta-analysis, indirect treatment comparison or network meta-analysis (frequentist or Bayesian) with patient-level and/or aggregate data from RCTs
•
Provide senior technical and statistical leadership and effective ad hoc problem-solving support to the delivery of diverse evidence synthesis projects
•
Edit, review, and develop scripts to ensure accurate and efficient implementation tailored to specific research problems. Full proficiency and demonstrable coding/programming experience in WinBUGS, OpenBUGS, JAGS and R is required, and knowledge of Stan is desirable
•
Provide technical guidance, input and quality control for key deliverables (e.g., draft protocols, statistical analysis plans, reports, manuscripts)
•
Support project implementation including overall project management and client engagement
Business development
•
Conceptualize evidence synthesis engagements in response to client request for proposals
•
Contribute to business development; build and maintain effective client relationships
Driving development
•
Establish research credentials and further the wider IQVIA profile in evidence synthesis through the development of innovative methods and the dissemination of research outputs in peer-reviewed journals and scientific conferences
•
Support the development of product offerings and internal process optimization as part of the Centre of Excellence for Indirect Treatment Comparisons
Mentoring
•
Coaching and training for junior statisticians and project delivery teams
•
Serve as a line manager for junior staff members
QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE, TECHNICAL AND PERSONAL SKILLLS
Essential qualifications
•
Master’s degree in (medical) statistics, biostatistics, mathematics, epidemiology, public health, health economics or related discipline
•
PhD in a subject related to health services research or statistics is desirable
Essential skills, knowledge and personal behaviours
•
At least 5 years prior relevant experience working as a statistician in consultancy, CRO, pharmaceutical/biotech or academia (as post-graduate researcher)
•
Strong quantitative skills and experience with Bayesian statistics, generalized linear models, feasibility assessments, direct and indirect treatment comparisons (ITCs), population-adjustment (MAIC, STC, ML-NMR), surrogate endpoint evaluation, structured expert elicitation, survival analyses
•
Strong programming skills in R and good command of Stan or WinBUGS/OpenBUGS/JAGS (other statistical software and decision support packages desirable), ability to provide evidence of this applied in a business or academic setting
•
Experience developing tools or automating processes used in ITCs or broader statistical workflows in HTA, preferably in R, Stan or any other relevant programming language.
•
Experience in clinical comparison across the evidence base (e.g., assessment of cross-trial heterogeneity in populations, interventions, outcomes and study design) and hands-on familiarity with tools to assess the quality and risk of bias of the included evidence (e.g., RoB-2, ROBINS-I, GRADE, AMSTAR-2)
•
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, including in the context of client strategic challenges
•
Excellent scientific writing skills. Publication track record is desirable but not necessary
•
Excellent oral communication skills and ability to convey technically complex issues to non-technical audiences and teams; prior coaching and training experience is desirable
•
Good understanding of related HEOR domains (e.g. systematic literature reviews, health economic modelling)
•
Good team-based interpersonal skills but also an ability to work independently
•
Strong attention to detail
•
Good project management skills with proven time management and organizational skills

Who We Are
FTI Consulting is the leading global expert firm for organizations facing crisis and transformation. We work with many of the world’s top multinational corporations, law firms, banks and private equity firms on their most important issues to deliver impact that makes a difference. From resolving disputes, navigating crises, managing risk and optimizing performance, our teams respond rapidly to dynamic and complex situations.
At FTI Consulting, you’ll work side-by side with leaders who have shaped history, helping solve the biggest challenges making headlines today. From day one, you’ll be an integral part of a focused team where you can make a real impact. You’ll be surrounded by an open, collaborative culture that embraces diversity, recognition, professional development and, most importantly, you.
Are you ready to make your impact?
About The Role
Are you ready to work inside complex business environments and help shape high-impact recommendations for leading Telecom, Media and Technology (TMT) clients across Europe?
As a Senior Consultant within FTI Consulting's Business Transformation team, you will join a vertically specialised practice with a strong functional focus on strategy, transformation and transactions.
You will be part of a close-knit team of more than 30 professionals serving European clients (Private Equity firms, global corporates and banks) from two dedicated TMT hubs in London and Barcelona. You will work alongside experienced consultants and recognised industry experts who will coach you in identifying client challenges, conducting rigorous analysis, and developing insights that inform decisions at board and investment committee level.
The role demands a sharp analytical mindset, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to manage multiple workstreams while delivering high-quality output under tight deadlines. You will typically work in small, high-performing teams that actively encourage collaboration, learning and ownership.
Our team brings together top-tier consultants and former industry executives to deliver practical, actionable solutions that drive sustainable performance and long-term value. You will contribute to projects spanning strategic planning through to hands-on execution. As trusted advisers, we work side-by-side with our clients from day one, not only designing strategies but helping ensure they are implemented and deliver measurable impact.
What You'll Do
• Support the day-to-day delivery of client projects, working alongside FTI colleagues, client personnel and other advisers on the engagement.
• Apply business, strategy, finance and analytical skills across a broad range of client situations; including, but not limited to, market sizing and forecasting, competitor and operational benchmarking, business plan assessment, and financial modelling.
• Conduct primary and secondary research on public and private companies, markets, technologies and regulatory developments across the TMT sector.
• Translate analysis into clear, structured messages and build client-ready outputs, ensuring consistency and accuracy across all deliverables.
• Sense-check results, identify the implication behind the numbers, and flag issues early.
• Manage your own workload against deadlines, communicate progress proactively, and act on feedback. We operate an apprenticeship model, so you should expect to receive and apply feedback continuously.
• Contribute to the practice beyond client work, including intellectual capital such as points of view and white papers, as well as credentials, pitches and proposals.

• Act as a day-to-day point of contact for mid-level client counterparts, building credibility through the quality and clarity of your work.
• Direct and review the work of Consultants and Interns, and provide constructive feedback as a role model to more junior colleagues.
• Take a leading drafting role on proposals and business development materials.
What You Will Need To Succeed
Basic Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Management, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics or a related field.
• Professional experience, including time in a consulting, strategy, transactions or comparable role.
• Demonstrable knowledge of, and/or genuine interest in, the Telecom, Media and Technology sector.
• Proficiency in the use of the Microsoft Office Suite, in particular Excel and PowerPoint, in a professional environment.
• Practical experience applying AI and GenAI tools to research, analysis or content production in a professional setting.
• Ability to travel to clients and FTI Consulting offices as needed.
Preferred Qualifications
• Master's in Business Administration degree
• Prior experience in management consulting or a professional services environment.

JR158816 Senior Statistical Analyst
ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.
As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.
Senior Statistical Analyst - Real World Evidence
We are currently seeking a Senior Statistical Analyst to join our Real World Evidence (RWE) team. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work on observational research studies, real-world data analyses, health outcomes research, and epidemiology projects that help generate evidence to support healthcare decision-making.
As a Senior Statistical Analyst, you will play a key role throughout the project lifecycle, from study design and statistical planning through to analysis, reporting, publication and client interaction. The role requires strong technical expertise in SAS programming, statistical methodology, and the interpretation of complex healthcare datasets.
What You Will Be Doing
• Support study conception, design, and protocol development for real-world evidence and observational research projects.
• Contribute to study start-up activities, including review and development of protocols, case report forms, and statistical methodologies.
• Write statistical methods sections of study protocols and develop statistical analysis plans.
• Perform sample size and power calculations.
• Review database specifications and participate in data review activities.
• Develop table, listing and figure shells and programming specifications.
• Lead the review and validation of raw and derived variables.
• Create and maintain derived datasets using SAS programming.
• Conduct statistical analyses using appropriate methodologies, including advanced and specialized statistical techniques such as longitudinal analyses, repeated measures, survival analyses, and other complex modelling approaches.
• Develop and validate SAS programs, macros, tables, listings, figures, and project deliverables.
• Lead quality control activities throughout programming and analysis processes.
• Manage and review internal and external data transfers.
• Produce project reports, statistical outputs, visualizations, tables and graphs for client delivery.
• Contribute to manuscripts, abstracts, conference presentations and peer-reviewed publications.
• Write methods and results sections for final reports and scientific publications.
• Communicate directly with clients, investigators and cross-functional teams regarding project deliverables and statistical requirements.
• Represent Statistical Analysis in proposal development and RFP activities.
• Participate in department initiatives, process improvements, SOP development and training activities.
• Deliver internal technical presentations and contribute to knowledge sharing within the team.
• Attend departmental meetings and support broader Real World Evidence research activities.
Your Profile
To be successful in this role, you will possess a strong statistical and programming background, together with experience working with healthcare, clinical, observational or real-world data.
Required Qualifications and Experience:
• Master's degree or PhD in Statistics, Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Mathematics, Data Science, Public Health, or a related quantitative discipline.
• Significant experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, healthcare research, or Real World Evidence environment.
• Advanced SAS programming experience is essential, including development of datasets, statistical analyses, macros, tables, listings and figures.
• Strong understanding of statistical methodologies and their practical application to healthcare and observational data.
• Experience developing Statistical Analysis Plans (SAPs) and analysis specifications.
• Knowledge of observational study design, epidemiology, health outcomes research, registries, claims databases, electronic health records, or other real-world data sources is highly desirable.
• Experience applying statistical techniques such as regression modelling, survival analysis, repeated measures analysis and other advanced methods.
• Ability to independently manage statistical deliverables while collaborating effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain complex statistical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Preferred Experience:
• Experience within a Real World Evidence, Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR), Epidemiology, or Data Analytics team.
• Experience authoring publications, abstracts, or conference presentations.
• Proficiency in additional programming languages such as R is advantageous.
Why Join the Real World Evidence Team?
You will be part of a collaborative team delivering high-impact research that helps shape healthcare decisions and improve patient outcomes globally. This role provides the opportunity to work on diverse, scientifically rigorous projects while developing deep expertise in real-world data, advanced analytics and evidence generation.
Please note: Strong SAS programming experience is a core requirement for this position and will be a key focus throughout the selection process.

Job Title
Senior DevOps Engineer
Job Description
The Role
Following extensive global expansion over several years and a drive to standardise common systems and platforms globally, PL Re is undertaking a major back-office transformation programme and has established a Divisional Data Team to develop and manage an enterprise-wide data solution, reporting services and to embed best practice data governance.
We are looking to appoint a DevOps Senior to contribute towards the DevOps function within the Divisional Data Team (DDT). DevOps is the highest-risk pillar of the data engineering operating model, owning CI/CD, database change management, environment control, release management and platform access. The role holder will be the single point of accountability for how change moves safely from an engineer’s branch into production.
The role reports to the AVP, Data Engineering, who is responsible for prioritizing, planning and driving forward the data engineering and transformation activities required. The role holder will build close working relationships with data engineering, testing, reporting, architecture and IT infrastructure teams across our operating geographies, and will be responsible for ensuring releases are controlled, auditable and repeatable.
Core Responsibilities
Azure DevOps platform ownership
•    Own the Azure DevOps organisation and project configuration for the Divisional Data Team, including projects, teams, security groups, service connections, variable groups and secure files.
•    Administer permissions and access models across repositories, pipelines, artefacts and libraries, ensuring segregation of duties between engineers, reviewers and approvers.
•    Manage build agents (including self-hosted agent pools), agent capacity, scaling and patching.
•    Use Azure Boards to plan, track and report DevOps work, and integrate work items with commits, pull requests and releases for traceability.
•    Manage Azure Artifacts feeds, package versioning and retention policies.
Git branching strategy and standards
•    Define, document and enforce the branching strategy across all repositories (for example trunk-based or GitFlow-style dev/SIT/UAT/production branches), including naming conventions and promotion paths.
•    Set and maintain branch policies: required reviewers, minimum approvals, linked work items, build validation, comment resolution and merge strategy (squash, rebase or merge commit).
•    Own the pull request process — review quality standards, approval routing, and clear rules on who may approve changes to which repository.
•    Define the release branching, tagging and versioning model, and the process for hotfixes and emergency fixes.
•    Own merge conflict resolution guidance, rebase and cherry-pick standards, and rollback procedures.
Git repository management
•    Create, structure and maintain repositories; define repository standards, folder structures, README and documentation requirements.
•    Manage repository security, path-based policies, protected branches, forks and cross-repository dependencies.
•    Implement and maintain pre-commit and pre-merge quality gates, including linting, formatting and automated tests.
•    Manage repository hygiene: history management, large file handling, retention, archiving and repository migration where required.
•    Ensure no secrets or credentials are committed to source control, supported by scanning and remediation processes.
Deployment and CI/CD
•    Design, build and maintain CI/CD pipelines (YAML-based) for Snowflake SQL, dbt models, Streamlit applications, stored procedures and supporting scripts.
•    Own database change management (DCM), including the transition to and operation of a state-based deployment approach across development, SIT, UAT and production.
•    Maintain consistent, reproducible environments and infrastructure-as-code, including configuration management across environments.
•    Implement automated testing, deployment gates, approvals and post-deployment validation within pipelines.
•    Ensure reliable rollback and recovery mechanisms for failed deployments.
Release management
•    Own the end-to-end release calendar and release process for the data platform, coordinating with delivery, testing and business stakeholders.
•    Chair or represent the team at change advisory and release approval forums; prepare and submit change records (including ECRs) with appropriate evidence.
•    Manage release readiness: entry and exit criteria, environment lock-downs, dependency management and go/no-go decisions.
•    Maintain a complete and auditable release trail linking requirements, code, approvals and deployments to satisfy internal control and audit requirements.
•    Conduct post-implementation reviews and drive continuous improvement in deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore.
Security, access and compliance
•    Own role-based access control (RBAC) design and administration across Snowflake and Azure DevOps, including role hierarchy, secrets management and privileged access.
•    Implement and maintain data masking and PII controls, with documented approvals for access to sensitive data.
•    Manage certificate renewals, artefact repository configuration and remediation of security scanning findings (for example Snyk and SonarQube).
•    Ensure IT controls and Business Control compliance requirements are embedded within the delivery and release process.
Qualifications & Experience
•    Deep, hands-on expertise with Azure DevOps — Repos, Pipelines (YAML), Boards, Artifacts, self-hosted agents and service connections.

The Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) will provide specialist ecological advice, assurance and site-based support across major infrastructure and construction projects throughout Scotland.
Reporting to the SHEQ Manager, the role will ensure construction activities are undertaken in accordance with Scottish environmental legislation, planning requirements, protected species licences, client requirements and project environmental commitments.
The role will have a strong field-based component, working alongside project management, construction and environmental teams to identify ecological constraints, develop practical mitigation and provide ECoW supervision of activities in environmentally sensitive locations.

• Otters.
• Badgers.
• Bats.

• Reptiles and amphibians.
• Breeding birds.

Surveys & Assessments

Construction Support
• Review RAMS and construction methodologies for ecological risks.

• Undertake pre-start ecological briefings and toolbox talks.
• Provide practical ecological advice to Site Managers, Engineers, Supervisors and subcontractors.
• Attend planning and construction meetings where ecological constraints could affect delivery.
Sensitive Habitats & Peatland
Support the protection and management of sensitive Scottish habitats including:
• Peatland and deep peat.
• Blanket bog.
• Wet heath.
• Ancient woodland.
• Native woodland.
• Riparian habitats.
• Freshwater environments.
• Protected and designated sites.
Support implementation and monitoring of habitat and peatland restoration and reinstatement requirements.
Designated Sites
Provide ecological support for projects potentially affecting:
• Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs).
• Special Areas of Conservation (SACs).
• Special Protection Areas (SPAs).
• Ramsar sites.
• National Nature Reserves.
• Ancient Woodland.
• Local Nature Conservation Sites.
Ensure project teams understand and implement controls associated with designated sites.
Biodiversity & Habitat Enhancement
• Support delivery of project biodiversity objectives.
• Identify opportunities for habitat enhancement and restoration.
• Monitor habitat reinstatement following construction.
• Support biodiversity monitoring programmes.
• Assist with development and implementation of Biodiversity Enhancement Plans and client commitments.
• Maintain evidence demonstrating delivery of ecological mitigation and enhancement measures.
Environmental Compliance
Provide ecological advice relating to applicable Scottish requirements including:
• Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
• Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004.
• Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011.
• Conservation (Natural Habitats, &c.) Regulations 1994, as amended.
• Protection of Badgers Act 1992.
• Environmental Authorisation (Scotland) Regulations 2018, where relevant.
• Applicable planning conditions, licences, consents and client requirements.
Maintain awareness of legislative changes and guidance affecting ecological management in Scotland.
Ecological Incidents
• Respond to ecological incidents and unexpected discoveries.
• Immediately advise project teams where protected species or previously unidentified ecological constraints are encountered.
• Support environmental incident investigations.
• Escalate significant issues to the SHEQ Manager and Environmental Manager.
• Support liaison with statutory bodies where required.
• Capture and communicate lessons learned.
Stakeholder Engagement
Develop effective relationships with clients, project teams, landowners, ecological consultants, local authorities and statutory bodies including NatureScot, SEPA and relevant planning authorities.

Job Description:
Financial Analyst – Originations
Purpose of the role
To provide dedicated financial screening, modelling and Investment Committee preparation support for acquisition opportunities across Pallas Software Group.  The role matures the financial insights on targets, so that every Portfolio Manager has early access to rigorous, consistent analysis that can advance the PQs and Modelling before handing across to the M&A Execution team for final checking and approvals.
The role sits within the Finance function already attached to the Pallas Portfolio, working across all Portfolio Managers. The resource is deployed flexibly to whichever Portfolio Manager has a live origination or diligence need at a given time, working under the direction of the Finance Director to prioritise across competing demands.
Scope of Coverage
• Verticals: all software verticals held across the Pallas Software Group portfolio. The role is not dedicated to any single vertical and takes direction from the Finance Director on where to prioritise effort.
• Geography: United Kingdom and Ireland as the core market, extending to other European geographies as individual Portfolio Managers' mandates require.
• Deal types: platform acquisitions and bolt, on acquisitions into existing business units, as directed by the relevant Portfolio Manager.
• Deal size: predominantly owner, managed and founder, led businesses below the size threshold that attracts a competitive banked process.
Key Responsibilities
Screening and origination support
• Screen inbound and adviser, introduced opportunities, from any part of the group, against group investment criteria and hurdle rates, recommending pursue, watch, list or pass with a written rationale.
• Maintain and refresh target maps and market intelligence for the verticals each Portfolio Manager is actively assessing, using public, paid and proprietary sources.
• Support Portfolio Managers' adviser and intermediary relationships by logging opportunities promptly and coordinating timely follow, up.
• Monitor market events, funding rounds, leadership changes, competitor acquisitions and distress signals and flag relevant opportunities to the appropriate Portfolio Manager.
Modelling, analysis and execution
• Build acquisition models from source data: revenue quality and recurring revenue analysis, customer cohort and churn analysis, maintenance and net revenue retention trends, normalised EBITDA, working capital, cash conversion, IRR and payback under base, downside and upside cases.
• Prepare Investment Committee papers and offer support material, investment thesis, valuation range and bridge, key risks, integration assumptions and returns scenarios.
• Support the central execution team and Portfolio Managers in coordinating due diligence workstreams across finance, legal, technical and people contributors; maintain the diligence tracker and issues log; translate findings into model and price adjustments.
• Support deal structuring: consideration split, earn, out mechanics and metric definition, deferred consideration, escrow and set, off, and operational ring, fence provisions.
• Track post, completion performance against the acquisition model and feed variances back into future underwriting, across all portfolios the role has supported.
Pipeline management and reporting.
• Own pipeline management jointly with the BD Manager: the BD Manager owns origination and outreach volume, this role owns the financial qualification and status of each target, and the two work from a shared, current view of the pipeline.
• Own the capturing of notes and information recorded in the group CRM, on behalf of whichever Portfolio Manager the work relates to.
• Produce a standing pipeline report for the Portfolio and Finance Director covering coverage by vertical and geography, stage conversion rates, and pipeline ageing across the group.
• Maintain a competitive and valuation reference set spanning the verticals in which the group is active.
Person Specification
Essential
• Minimum of 2 years experience in a financial analysis role with direct exposure to M&A: transaction services, corporate development, lower midmarket M&A, or growth/debt finance
• Genuine modelling capability — able to build an acquisition model from messy management accounts and a trial balance without a template, and to defend the assumptions in front of an Investment Committee.
• Understanding of software business economics: recurring revenue, retention and expansion, gross margin structure, implementation and services drag, and hosting costs.
• Comfortable working across multiple stakeholders and priorities at once, taking direction from the Finance Director on where to focus effort at any given time.
• Credible with a Portfolio Manager and a founder's finance director in the same week. Writes clearly and concisely.
• Self, directing, with sound judgement on when to escalate and when to proceed.
•
Desirable
• Exposure to vertical market software, in any sector.
• Experience in a buy, and, build, holding company or serial, acquirer environment with a high, volume, small, ticket deal model.
• Familiarity with earn out design and post, acquisition performance measurement.
• Working knowledge of share purchase agreements, disclosure letters and warranty and indemnity insurance, sufficient to work effectively with counsel rather than to replace them.
• Additional European languages considered a bonus

PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here
PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.
About AI for Health
PATH’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative is our flagship technical team working across divisions to deliver best-in-class evaluation and implementation of AI in health, spanning model evaluation to product development and service innovation. We aim to use AI to address the world’s largest health inequities.
We’re looking for a clinician with research experience to help deliver PATH’s work evaluating whether different AI models and products can provide safe and effective mental health/wellbeing support for those most in need. You will collaborate with leading AI evaluation labs and with clinical, research, lived experience, and policy experts across sub-Saharan Africa and the UK to develop new ways of contextualising evaluation so that we can better understand what works, for whom, and in which contexts. You’ll bring clinical expertise to the design and execution of our evaluations, as well as coordinate day-to-day delivery across an international consortium. This role is a strong fit for an early-career clinician who wants their work to change how AI is built and used for mental health.
Responsibilities:
Bring Clinical Expertise to Evaluation
• Contribute to evaluation design, including which AI systems we test, who we test them for, how we test them, and how we learn from our partners to refine our approach. Keep this all current as the field evolves.
• Ground our simulated users/patients and automated (LLM) judges in clinical practice: help our partners specify personas and presentations and draft behaviour rubrics, and review transcripts for clinical errors before they go to the panels of clinicians and lived experience experts in each country. Expect to work hands-on alongside our partners.
• Lead PATH’s evaluation of consumer AI products, from general-purpose assistants to dedicated mental health apps, while tailoring evaluations to specific populations, cultures, and languages. Coordinate with developers on evaluation of their models and products.
• Co-author research on new methods for contextualised AI evaluation with consortium partners, bringing clinical expertise to how we build and validate simulated users/patients and LLM-judges.
Coordinate Delivery across the Consortium
• Coordinate day-to-day delivery across our partners in South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, the UK, and the US (each of whom leads their own strand of the work): work with our ops team to track progress, organise working meetings, follow up on actions, and solve problems as they appear.
• Matrix manage members of the AI4Health team supporting the delivery of consumer AI product evaluations, including both fellows doing their PhDs (whom you will contribute to the supervision of), as well as peers leading engineering for the programme.
• Contribute to donor reports and to presentations for funders and external audiences.
Publish Evidence
• Prepare content for a website presenting all results of PATH’s AI evaluations in mental health, including plain-language summaries for people seeking support; contribute to writing seminal reports on the state of AI safety and effectiveness for global mental health; and support presentation of evidence to international commissions and panels.
• Write up our results for high-impact academic venues and established policy fora.
Contribute to the Broader AI programme
• Support research and related activities led by other members of the AI team (where your expert skill set is relevant, and sometimes just as another pair of hands), including the soon-to-be-launched ‘Nature Commission on Consumer AI and Wellbeing’ for which PATH is hosting the secretariat.
• This is a full-time post based in London. You’ll report to PATH’s Deputy Director for AI for Health. This role includes international travel to partner sites and convenings (around 10–15% of time).
Required Skills and Experience
• A professional qualification in a clinical discipline (e.g., clinical psychology, medicine, mental health nursing, or equivalent), with hands-on clinical experience in mental health (including training placements or rotations).
• Research experience, with evidence of scientific writing (e.g., publications, preprints, or a doctoral thesis).
• Expertise/experience in measurement and evaluation methods—reliability, validity, inter-rater agreement.
• Some programming experience (e.g., Python or R), and hands-on use of LLMs (e.g., writing prompts, or writing and testing rubrics).
• Excellent written and verbal communication for scientific, clinical, public, and policy audiences.
• Ability to coordinate work and deadlines across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
Preferred Qualifications
• Two+ years’ clinical experience in mental health since qualifying.
• Research experience in digital mental health or experience evaluating digital health products (including their clinical safety).
• Experience working with collaborators or patients in low- and middle-income countries, ideally in sub-Saharan Africa.
• Experience coordinating a multi-partner or multi-site research program.
• Research experience in simulating users or patients with LLMs, validating automated judges against human raters, or building LLM-based evaluation pipelines.
• Experience of industry engagement and/or evaluation governance.
• Experience working with lived experience or patient and public involvement panels.
We know great candidates won’t always meet every listed qualification. Research shows that some groups, on average, are more likely to self-select out if they feel they don’t meet all requirements. If you’re excited about the role and think you’d be a good fit, we encourage you to apply.

What if you could work with remarkable people on extraordinary things? What if the end result was something a little bit special? What if your role was mission critical?
For over 75 years, AWE has been at the forefront of nuclear weapons research and development. We have a critical mission: to provide the warheads for the UK's ultimate deterrent, Trident. Materials Science supports the life cycle of warhead components and technologies to ensure the reliability of the UK's strategic deterrent and national security mission. A nuclear warhead contains metals, ceramics, inorganic salts, rubbers, foams, adhesives, high explosives and radioactive substances. Engineer the safety net that protects millions
The Chief Security Office helps us move fast without compromising security, resilience or control.
It protects our people, customers, data and technology while building security into the products, platforms and journeys people use every day.
And as a Cyber Security Engineer graduate, your work will be nothing short of impactful. You’ll work in the enabling layer of CSO, doing the hard yards of reducing cyber risk at every level. That includes designing and building controls, tooling, detection logic and securing systems that protect millions.
Two years. Real impact
Throughout this two-year scheme, you’ll go beyond just putting out fires. Your work will be centred on secure design, detection capability and risk reduction – as you build security into the bones of every system, platform and delivery process.
​Expect to:
• Build and improve security tools and services that help us innovate and safely go faster
• Create solutions that protect customers, colleagues and data from cyber threats

What your work could look like
• Helping engineering teams embed security into every design and deliverable

Daily collaboration with the application development and cloud platform teams to plan and prioritise security requirements as part of the secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC).

Recommending security best practices for cloud platforms and automating compliance with cloud security baselines (e.g. CIS Benchmarks).

Implementation of automated security tooling (e.g. within a Continuous Integration (CI) pipeline) to validate security requirements and identify potential issues.

Working with external organisations to plan, scope and facilitate penetration tests.

Reviewing the outputs from security tools and security practices. You will filter and prioritise these into security stories that can be understood and actioned by the delivery teams.
•
Verifying the implementation of security principles, architectural patterns, and requirements.
•
Driving the adoption of cyber security practices (e.g. vulnerability management, threat modelling etc.) within Agile delivery teams.
•
Putting people first & developing others – You’ll help coach and develop more junior members of the team.

•
Experience of implementing application security or Cloud platform security.
•
Experience in Defence Sector
•
Active Security Clearance
•
A detailed understanding of web application security.
•
An understanding of modern cryptography and its application for encryption in-transit, encryption at-rest, hashing and digital signatures.
•
An understanding of security practices such as threat modelling, vulnerability management, application security testing, and penetration testing.
•
Experience of integrating application security tools (e.g. static analysis, dynamic analysis etc.) into the SSDLC.
•
Experience of using modern version control systems (e.g. git) and either a scripting language (e.g. Bash, Powershell etc.), or a programming language (e.g. Python, Java, .NET, JS etc.), or an Infrastructure as Code language (e.g. Terraform, ARM Templates, Ansible etc.) to automate tasks.

The ability to convey security issues to technical and non-technical people.

•
An industry recognised qualification in Cyber Security.
•
AWS or Azure mid-level certifications.
•
Participation in the cyber security community (e.g. OWASP, HackTheBox, CTFs etc.).
•
Experience working with agile software development methodologies (e.g. Scrum or Kanban).

Adaptation & Resilience Pricing Analyst
Location: London
Contract Type: Permanent
Work Pattern: Full Time and Hybrid
MS Amlin’s ESG Re team is expanding rapidly to meet demand for innovative (re)insurance solutions that build resilience to climate risks, nature loss, socio-economic fragility and other systemic risks. We are seeking a commercially astute Risk Assessment & Pricing Specialist (actuarial, analytical, modelling or reinsurance pricing background) to build technical capability and scale global growth.
At MS Amlin, Sustainability is integral to how we grow profitably and responsibly, balancing business value with societal impact and the environment. Our goal is to make resilience insurable, scalable and commercially sustainable. This role suits someone who enjoys collaborating on complex risks while contributing to profitable growth and positive impact.
This role will act as the dedicated risk assessment and pricing capability for ESG Re and will be closely aligned with the Actuarial Pricing team. You will support the Head of Sustainability, ESG Re team, and Reinsurance function, applying structured analysis to emerging market risks, where insurance affordability and availability remain limited.
You will combine quantitative analysis with commercial judgment, supporting new revenue streams and deliver commercially grounded solutions. The role contributes to closing the global protection gap while enabling resilience and long-term value creation.
About the Job
As a Risk & Pricing Specialist, you’ll be at the forefront of supporting underwriting with technically robust, commercially informed insights, particularly across innovative resilience and adaptation solutions, spanning climate change, nature loss, evolving global health, conflict and migration and other systemic risks. While no two days are alike, here’s a snapshot of key responsibilities:
• Assess technical submissions spanning climate, nature, health, conflict & systemic risks, including exposure evaluation, structure review, expected loss estimation & rate-on-line guidance.
• Analyse data to build robust, transparent risk assessments & pricing approaches that support business objectives & enable scalable, commercially viable solutions.
• Challenge data, assumptions, catastrophe outputs & pricing methodologies to ensure technical rigour & alignment with MS Amlin’s view of risk and its Sustainability Strategy.
• Act as a trusted technical advisor to the Head of Sustainability & Senior Underwriters, offering insight into expected loss calculations, pricing & renewal considerations, and treaty and portfolio structures including layer terms, loss histories & accumulation
• Translate unconventional or development-driven proposals into clear, insurable structures with disciplined pricing, strengthening ESG Re's ability to convert pipeline opportunities into bound business.
• Support the ESG Re Team in structuring innovative products (parametric, index-based, blended-finance-backed, sovereign risk pools, community schemes) that support adaptation finance and inclusive growth.
• Support market engagement by preparing technical insights for discussions with brokers, multilaterals, NGOs & humanitarians; help articulate our pricing rationale, risk appetite & product value propositions in the context of systemic risk reduction.
• Work cross-functionally across pricing, model development, data improvement and wider Sustainability initiatives.
You’re going to enjoy this job if you:
• Are motivated by the opportunity to create long-term, sustainable enterprise value by deploying commercially grounded underwriting, with a strong focus on adaptation finance, to build resilience in vulnerable communities.
• Maintain strong curiosity with industry trends, catastrophe modelling, climate-related risk developments and emerging best practices, particularly where models do not currently exist and new data partnerships / proxy data may be required.
• Have an entrepreneurial mindset and are excited by building new markets, not just operating in established ones.
• Have a passion for problem-solving and interrogating complex, unconventional datasets.
• Collaborate naturally across underwriting, actuarial, modelling, and analytics functions with the aim of improving technical processes, models and approaches.
What you’ll need:
For this particular role there are some important qualifications and experience we need you to have. These include:
Essential:
• Experience in (re)insurance pricing, risk analysis, catastrophe modelling, or reinsurance underwriting.
• Strong capability in interpreting complex datasets, evaluating reinsurance structures and performing technical risk assessments.
• Confidence in challenging assumptions, pricing methodologies and modelled and non modelled outputs in emerging or data constrained environments.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.

You will lead our responsible deployment agenda for AVEVA’s AI software products and for adoption of AI within AVEVA’s operations.  Our responsible AI agenda is grounded in a set of core principles: sustainability; accuracy and robustness; human-centricity and fairness; data governance and privacy; transparency and explainability; and accountability.

Responsible deployment is core to AVEVA’s Industrial AI agenda, and this role will balance external engagement with internal governance. Externally, you will work with customers, industry bodies, standards organisations, and public sector stakeholders to shape practical governance and accountability approaches for safe, secure, and sustainable AI in industrial operations, across regulated, safety- and mission-critical industrial environments. Internally, you will help to convert those expectations into scalable policies, controls, and decision processes that product and engineering teams can adopt.
You will partner closely with our Product, Enterprise IT, Security, Sustainability, Legal, Risk and Talent and Learning teams, while remaining accountable for responsible deployment in policy design, stakeholder engagement, and enterprise learning enablement.

As a technical leader, you’ll work with senior stakeholders to agree architectural principles and strategic direction, develop customer relationships and account management, and feed what you learn on the ground back into our product direction. You’ll manage, coach and develop a small number of staff, with a focus on performance and career development, whilst advising on new technologies and approaches to AI and helping the people around you learn, develop and grow.

Leading Frontier AI projects – You’ll be the technical lead on customer engagements, owning the solution end to end and guiding a team of Forward Deployed Engineers to deliver it.

Working directly with customers – You’ll work with customers and senior stakeholders to understand their business problems and desired outcomes, and agree architectural principles and strategic direction.

Active participation in technology communities and knowledge sharing, internally and externally.

VIAVI AI RSG is a city-scale digital twin of a mobile network. The simulation engine that models cell sites, connected devices, and radio behaviour.

A REST framework and React-based UI powering the product.
•
Our own SDK (ADK) for rApp/xApp development.
•
An AI Expert LLM built directly into the product for natural-language querying, scenario creation, and analysis.

Demonstrated skills in time management and ability work in a collaborative/team environment.

Capability to quickly adapt to new projects and changing priorities when needed.

Ability/Desire to work on a temporary assignment in another country/location.

Proactive mindset, strong initiative, and a demonstrated drive to take ownership and make things happen.

Curiosity and a willingness to learn, ask questions, seek feedback, and continuously develop technical and leadership capabilities.

Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across teams and engage with people from different technical backgrounds.

Ability to quickly adapt to new projects, changing priorities, and unfamiliar challenges when needed.

Demonstrated leadership potential, including the ability to influence others, take responsibility, and contribute positively to team outcomes, regardless of formal leadership experience.

Resilience and perseverance when faced with ambiguity, setbacks, or technically challenging problems.

Ability to operate with a high degree of independence while knowing when to seek guidance or involve others.

One component is a “sensor”, which is a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network can correlate malicious behavior across multiple machines and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.
Join CrowdStrike and become a key leader in building the most innovative endpoint security solution in the world.  Our sensor development team is responsible for building the endpoint sensor which deploys on multiple platforms including Windows, Mac, and Linux. You will be required to assist with architecting solutions and support in implementing our core features. Features will cross-cut most core OS subsystems such as file system, memory and process, and networking.

About Ofcom
As the UK’s communications regulator, we’re delivering vital work that helps keep the UK connected and shapes the future of how we’ll stay connected with each other.
Our work covers everything from phones and broadband, through to TV, radio, the postal service, and wireless devices. We’re also taking on the challenge of making the online world a safer place. And we need people of all backgrounds, skill sets, and experiences to help us achieve our goal of making communications work for everyone.
Team overview
Ofcom’s mission is to make communications work for everyone. We are looking for an experienced media manager to join our busy media relations team, and to help explain how our work affects people up and down the country.
Ofcom is the regulator for the communications services that we use and rely on each day. We regulate services from phone and broadband to TV and radio, airwaves and the postal service. And we’ve taken on new duties to make online services safer for everyone, with work underway to implement the UK’s forthcoming social media ban. It’s important work on behalf of people across the UK.
In joining our fast-paced, welcoming and expert Communications Department, you’ll see why Ofcom was previously named by PR Week as the UK’s best place for communications professionals to work in-house.
Purpose of the Role
We’re looking for an enthusiastic and experienced media communicator with a strong news sense and an excellent understanding of journalists’ demands.
The role will involve communicating some of our most high-profile, wide-ranging work, which makes national news on a daily basis. That might include topics like creating a safer life online for children and adults in the UK; enforcing standards in TV and radio; holding telecoms firms to account; and helping the UK to be at the cutting edge of new technology.
You will need shrewd judgement and initiative to help Ofcom shape and influence opinions in the modern news environment. You’ll be an expert in judging reputational risk, have strong networking skills, and be a consummate multi-tasker - calmly balancing reactive and proactive communications priorities. You’ll also work with our digital news team to bring our story to life for the public, consumer groups, politicians and policy-makers and media.
Key responsibilities
• Take a leading role in responding to enquiries from all sections of the media – often national print, online and broadcast, and also international, regional, specialist and trade.
• Build and sustain effective relationships with media and other external stakeholders.
• Help to develop and enhance Ofcom's media profile by identifying proactive opportunities and generating positive coverage.
• Develop a strong understanding of relevant fields of Ofcom’s work, over time, becoming an expert within the Communications team on specific policy and subject areas.
• Manage Ofcom’s external announcements pipeline and weekly reporting on the Communications team’s activity to senior leaders.
Essential Skills, knowledge and experience
• Excellent understanding of the media and requirements of journalists.
• Executing Plans: Proven track record of managing completing priorities in a fast-paced, high-profile press office environment
• Strong appetite for media relations, together with a sharp news sense and the ability to identify positive consumer angles with media appeal.
• Building Solutions: Analytical and strategic mindset, able to cut through complex issues to see the wider picture.
• Articulating Ideas: Clear, calm communicator. Excellent writing skills, and the ability to convert complex policy into plain English.
• Quick learner, flexible and enthusiastic about working across a range of communications issues.
• Knowledge of the latest digital communications trends and techniques.
• An ability to identify with, and embody, Ofcom's values of excellence, agility, empowerment, collaboration and respect.
• Understanding of, or familiarity with, Ofcom’s regulated industries (in particular online safety) would be an advantage.
Inclusive hiring at Ofcom
At Ofcom, our mission is clear: to make communications work for everyone. To achieve that, our people must reflect the diversity of the UK, in background, identity and experience.
We believe innovation thrives when difference is valued and everyone feels empowered to contribute their ideas and perspectives. That’s why we welcome colleagues of all ethnicities and races, sexes, genders and gender identities, sexual orientations, ages, faiths and beliefs, and those with apparent and non‑apparent disabilities. We value socio‑economic diversity, life experience and neurodiversity too. Whether you’re a carer, a parent, a veteran, or re‑entering work after time away, your voice and perspective matter here.
Flexibility is at the heart of how we work because we want you to thrive in a way that suits you best. Most roles can therefore be adapted for part‑time hours, job shares, or other flexible arrangements. Learn more about our Rewards, Benefits and Wellbeing on our careers page.
Our recruitment process is intentionally designed to be open and accessible. If you need adjustments, information in a different format or an alternative way to apply, contact us at resourcing@ofcom.org.uk or 0330 912 1378.
As a proud Disability Confident Leader, we guarantee interviews for disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for a role. You can read more about this commitment here.
Whoever you are, whatever your story, you belong at Ofcom.

Job Description:
Department
The Short-Term Analytical Team
Position purpose
The role is based in London. In order for EDF Trading to maximise the return from the month-ahead to day-ahead wholesale power markets, either from EDF generation assets or through proprietary trading, the traders require detailed, commercially focussed analysis produced on a timely basis.
In the front office, working closely with both the short-term analysts in charge of EDF portfolio optimisation in Paris and the power traders in London, the Short-Term Power Market Analyst has a dual role covering both operational and development duties.
Moreover, the analyst is expected to take distance from the operational activity and our modelling in order to identify areas of improvement and contribute to the definition of the objectives of the team. He/She must participate to the training of junior analysts.
Main Operational Responsibilities
Market Analysis:
• Provide data analytics and risk analysis on short term power market to the desk
• Support the Short-Term desk for the price forecasts and trading strategies
EDF system risk analysis:
• Follow the Day-Ahead and Week-Ahead optimisation shifts
• Communicate time critical information to the traders in London
• Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including REMIT, through the consistent application of defined processes.
Main Development/Modelling Responsibilities
The short-term power market analyst is responsible of the whole life cycle of an application or a model: from the research/design to the development/implementation and the maintenance.
The analyst is autonomous on his/her projects and is responsible of critical applications.
Example of models/applications/solutions:
• Fundamental and quantitative (statistical, data science driven) models to better anticipate market behaviour and improve price forecasting models. All components of the market could be addressed like load forecast, competitors’ orders, availabilities, etc...
• Automation of workflows
• Data visualisation via powerBI or web applications
The analyst is also responsible in improving robustness of the applications of the team by adding unit tests on critical parts of the applications and refactoring unstable functions he/she uses in his projects. The analyst must take part actively to the peer reviews of the junior analysts in order to share good practises.
Experience required
Ability to work under pressure, timeliness, accuracy and the ability to understand the wider commercial implications of the work are critical to be successful in this position.
The analyst will use his/her expertise to support the short-term power traders while at the same time ensuring an effective operational relationship with the asset managers at EDF. He/she will be expected to take the initiative to continuously improve existing processes, tools and models with the aim of improving the overall management of the EDF portfolio and wholesale market positions.
It is as well necessary to be proactive in the research of market modelling improvements to succeed in this position.
Technical requirements
Fluent in French & English
Educated to master’s degree level, preferably with a high statistics or mathematics component
Experience of building/developing stochastic or deterministic optimisation procedures/models
Advanced skills in:
• Data science
• Python (Api, Data management, statistical modelling)
• Web development (javascript)
• Source code management (Git)
Full understanding of the ways of working of the power market:
• Power asset management and optimisation
• Power market coupling algorithm
Person specification
As well as having strong analytical skills, attention to detail and enthusiasm the candidate needs to have a commercial approach to his/her duties. Similarly, a flexible approach to problem solving and the ability to work under pressure are essential.
Applicants for the role will also be expected to have strong communications skills with the confidence to work effectively with both power traders and asset managers.
Hours of work:
40 hours per week, Monday to Friday

• Managing and negotiating complex supplier contracts, ensuring compliance with legal requirements and company policies;
• Collaborating effectively with Multi-Functional Teams (MFTs) including engineering, production, quality, and legal departments to ensure alignment on procurement strategies and project goals;
