To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
KLA has manufacturing sites worldwide. The Global Operations (GOPS) team, comprised of Manufacturing, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing Engineering, Installation and Quality, builds our leading-edge technology. GOPS partners with KLA's global supply base and design engineering teams to develop new products, working continuously to build better, faster and more cost-efficient solutions.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
At KLA SensArray, we manufacture highly specialised semiconductor metrology & inspection equipment used by leading semiconductor manufacturers worldwide. Based at our state-of-the-art facility in Newport, South Wales, this role offers the opportunity to work in a clean, precision manufacturing environment where attention to detail and craftsmanship are critical to product quality.
As the dedicated Quality Control (QC) Technician you will provide independent quality inspection and verification across the SensArray manufacturing process, covering incoming materials, in-process production activity, and final outgoing product release.
The role is responsible for ensuring that products, components, substrates, documentation, cleanliness standards, meet defined requirements before progressing through production.
Your Day-to-Day Responsibilities
Incoming Quality Control
• Inspect incoming materials, substrates, components, consumables, and supplier documentation against defined specifications.
• Confirm correct part numbers, revision levels, quantities, packaging condition, and traceability requirements.
• Identify, quarantine, and escalate non-conforming or suspect material before release to production.
• Maintain accurate incoming inspection records and support supplier quality follow-up where required.
In-Process Quality Control
• Perform quality checks across SensArray production lines, including High Temp, Etch Temp, TC, RTD, and DISIS, to confirm products and processes meet applicable standards.
• Verify operators are working on current SOPs, work instructions, process controls, and quality requirements.
• Conduct routine quality gates, process audits, and workmanship checks during key manufacturing stages.
• Monitor ESD, cleanliness, documentation, and product handling standards across the production area.
• Support containment activity and stop escalation when quality risks are identified.
Outgoing Quality Control
• Complete final inspection of finished products before shipment.
• Review product quality records, test data, manufacturing documentation, labelling, and traceability.
• Confirm products meet customer, internal, packaging, and shipping requirements before release.
• Approve, reject, or escalate product release decisions based on inspection outcome.
Non-Conformance & Quality Improvement
• Raise and support Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) for identified defects or process failures.
• Assist with containment, root cause investigation, corrective action, and preventive action activity.
• Track recurring issues, quality trends, and defect data to support continuous improvement.
• Work with Production, Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams to reduce risk and improve process capability.
Skills & Experience
Essential
• Previous Quality Control or Quality Assurance experience within an electronics manufacturing environment.
• Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, work instructions, and quality requirements.
• Experience performing visual, dimensional, documentation, or final product inspections.
• Strong attention to detail with the confidence to challenge non-conforming work.
• Competent in Microsoft Office and ERP systems.
Desirable
• Experience in semiconductor, electronics, clean manufacturing, or high-reliability production environments.
• Knowledge of ESD controls, cleanroom practices, ISO 9001 quality systems, SPC, and quality metrics.
• Experience using microscopes, metrology equipment, or other inspection tools.
• Understanding of root cause analysis and continuous improvement methodologies.
Qualifications
• HNC qualification or equivalent technical qualification would be advantageous
What will we offer you?
This is a permanent position working Monday to Friday.
KLA benefits include - Annual leave starting at 25 days (plus bank holidays), contributory pension scheme, cash health plan, cycle to work scheme, global bonus plan, share scheme, rewards scheme, life assurance and overtime premiums.
Minimum Qualifications
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Use of AI Statement
At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset.
We offer a competitive, family friendly total rewards package. We design our programs to reflect our commitment to an inclusive environment, while ensuring we provide benefits that meet the diverse needs of our employees.

We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. •

What if your tax expertise could do more than manage compliance — what if it could help change patients' lives?
It might not be the first thing that comes to mind when you think about a tax role but at Bristol Myers Squibb, everything connects back to our purpose: transforming patients' lives through science. And the team that keeps our tax operations running with precision and integrity? They're part of that story too.
We're looking for a Senior Tax Manager to join our European Tax Centre of Excellence (COE) in Chester - a role where your technical skills meet real business influence and where the work you do every day genuinely matters.
This is a tax role with real breadth. And real accountability for the outcomes across your markets.
Here's what makes this different from a standard in-house tax position: you won't be a cog in a machine, processing the same returns year after year.
You'll lead a portfolio of European markets and direct a team of tax professionals - working closely with local finance teams and external advisers to high-quality processes. You'll be the expert your finance colleagues come to when they need clarity, the professional who challenges external advisers on both direct tax and VAT matters, the senior lead who manages tax audits through to resolution, and the person who translates complex legislation into practical action to guide our stakeholders
Here's what your role will actually look like:
• You'll run the full direct tax cycle for your own markets - leading corporate income tax return preparation with local external advisers, applying genuine technical challenge to their work, managing tax authority audits and enquiries through to resolution, drawing on your working knowledge of VAT where indirect tax questions arise, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks.
• You'll gain hands-on US GAAP experience - preparing and submitting US tax reporting including quarterly current and deferred tax provisions using TaxStream technology. This isn't something most in-house European tax roles offer, and it's a genuine differentiator for your CV.
• You'll work across the full breadth of tax governance - staying on top of evolving regulatory requirements across your markets, including the evolving world of Pillar Two.
• You'll be a genuine internal consultant - advising finance and business stakeholders on tax matters, explaining complex technical requirements in language they can act on, and building the kind of trusted relationships that make you indispensable.
• You'll coach and assist in developing a team of tax professionals - setting objectives, coaching technical development, and building a team that delivers to a consistently high standard across your markets.
• You'll shape how tax is done, not just do it - contributing to the COE's strategy around standardisation, automation, and continuous improvement. If you're curious about tax technology and smarter ways of working, this team is actively investing in that space.
• You'll stay ahead of legislative change - monitoring developments across your markets, analysing their impact, and proactively communicating what matters to the people who need to know.
What do you actually gain from joining this team?
Let's talk about what this role opens up for you - concretely.
Breadth that most tax roles simply don't offer. European direct tax, US GAAP reporting, transfer pricing exposure, Pillar Two - all under one role, in one team. Whether you're looking to deepen your specialism or broaden your horizons, this role does both.
Access to leading external advisers. You won't be working in isolation. You'll collaborate with top-tier advisory firms, learn from their expertise, and develop the skills to challenge and manage them effectively - experience that builds your professional credibility significantly.
Real stakeholder visibility. You'll regularly engage with senior finance leaders and business partners globally. That kind of cross-functional, international exposure builds commercial acumen and communication skills that go far beyond technical tax knowledge.
Flexible, hybrid working from our modern office in Chester. A. With the 50% hybrid-working model, you’ll get to collaborate and build supportive working relationships with the large tax team, as well as others in the ECC, whilst creating a healthy work-life balance.
The BMS mission as your backdrop. When you're filing that return, managing that audit, or navigating a piece of new legislation — you're doing it in support of a company that is genuinely working to help patients with serious diseases. That context changes how the work feels.
You'll thrive in this role if…
• You're a qualified accountant and/or chartered tax adviser (CTA, ACA, ACCA or equivalent) with solid experience in tax accounting, tax provisioning, and statutory audit support.
• You have hands-on tax audit experience, having led or managed enquiries with tax authorities, and a good working knowledge of VAT.
• You have experience coaching and developing people, with a track record of managing, coaching and growing tax professionals.
• You've managed external advisers and you know how to review compliance deliverables with the right level of technical rigour.
• You communicate confidently - able to break down complex tax matters for finance colleagues and non-tax stakeholders alike, without losing accuracy.
• You're genuinely interested in tax technology, process improvement, and automation and you see them as opportunities, not threats.
• You're organised, ownership-driven, and comfortable managing multiple markets and deadlines simultaneously.
• You're fluent in English - additional European languages are a bonus, but not a requirement.
Don't tick every single box? We'd still love to hear from you. If you believe you could succeed in this role, that matters to us and we mean it.

At Rolls‑Royce SMR, our mission is to deliver clean, affordable energy for all. Our Small Modular Reactor (SMR) programme is a British solution to a global energy challenge, designed to accelerate decarbonisation while supporting energy security. We are uniquely positioned to become a world leader in SMR technology and one of the UK’s most exciting green export opportunities—combining proven nuclear engineering with advanced modular manufacturing to transform how low‑carbon power is delivered.
The Team
You’ll be joining the Materials & Chemistry team. This cross‑functional group supports the entire lifecycle of the RR‑SMR—from concept design to decommissioning—providing essential expertise across Reactor Plant & Systems, Components & Mechanical Equipment, Manufacturing Engineering, the Conventional Island, and both internal and external supply chain stakeholders. Your contribution will help shape the safety, integrity, and performance of the SMR design.
Role Summary
We are recruiting a Senior Materials Engineer – Welding & Manufacturing, a key technical role responsible for developing, assuring, and integrating the welding and manufacturing requirements that underpin the RR‑SMR design. This role is essential to ensuring that all structural materials, welds, special processes, and manufacturing routes meet our expectations for nuclear‑grade integrity. You will act as a technical partner to our supply chain, and a trusted advisor within multidisciplinary engineering teams. Your contribution will significantly influence compliance, manufacturability, and long‑term plant safety.
Key Responsibilities
You will be doing…
•
Leading the development and delivery of material specifications and providing expert manufacturing support.
•
Acting as technical partner for suppliers who design and manufacture metallic components—reviewing and approving Methods of Manufacture, documentation packs, data cards, and final documentation.
•
Supporting the design and welding teams on weld consumable specification, supply, and control.
•
Conducting or supporting special process audits (such as heat treatment, forging, welding) and maintaining oversight of supplier special processes and non‑conformance resolution.
•
Collaborating closely with internal engineering and project stakeholders, representing RR‑SMR with suppliers and industry bodies.
The Impact
In this role, you will directly contribute to the integrity and manufacturability of the RR‑SMR’s key components. Your expertise ensures that welded structures, fabrication processes, and material properties meet stringent nuclear requirements. This role influences safety, schedule, supply chain readiness, and component performance—making it a high‑impact opportunity to shape how SMRs are manufactured and delivered.
Essential Qualifications & Experience
To succeed in this role, you will bring:
•
A degree (or equivalent) in a relevant engineering discipline (materials, welding, mechanical, manufacturing, etc.).
•
Strong understanding of materials systems, their behaviour, and intended nuclear uses.
•
Practical experience in materials manufacturing, including interpretation of manufacturing routes, special process controls, forging, fabrication, welding, post‑weld heat treatment, and documentation packs.
•
Experience supporting or conducting technical audits of special processes.
•
Experience working in a regulated industry, ideally nuclear or power generation. (Experience with PWR environments, ALARP/BAT, and ASME compliance beneficial.)
•
Strong communication skills and proven ability to present technical information clearly to diverse stakeholders.
Location & Working Pattern
We offer a flexible hybrid working model. This role can be based in Derby, Warrington or Manchester, with the frequency of office attendance agreed during the recruitment process based on individual and business needs.
Pay and Benefits
We anticipate paying a salary of between £50,650 - £66,500 plus:-
•
Bonus - Performance related target opportunity 12.5%

Benefits Allowance – £2,200 per annum, enabling you to create a bespoke package
•
Pension - 12% employer and 6% employee contributions.
•
Holidays - 28 days holiday (+ public holidays) and the ability to buy or sell up to 4 days.
•
Private Medical Insurance - BUPA single cover health care
•
Life Assurance - 6x pensionable pay
•
£250 - One-off payment for new starters for home office purchases

You’ll be joining a forward-thinking organisation that values transparency, fairness, and innovation. We offer:

•    Opportunities for career growth in a rapidly scaling business.
•    A culture that values diversity, innovation, and continuous learning.

Please only apply for one internship position, choosing the role that best matches your skills and interests. We'll consider your application across all of our research opportunities where appropriate.
We tackle the most complex problems in quantitative finance, by bringing scientific clarity to financial complexity.
From our London HQ, we unite world-class researchers and engineers in an environment that values deep exploration and methodical execution - because the best ideas take time to evolve.  Together we’re building a world-class platform to amplify our teams’ most powerful ideas.
Join a research team where curiosity meets scale. You’ll investigate foundational questions, uncover market insights and push the boundaries of what's possible - all with the support of near-limitless compute and world-class peers.
Take the next step in your career.
The role
• 10-week summer programme (21st June - 27th August 2027)
• 09:00-17:30 working hours
• Based in Central London
Over the course of 10 weeks, G-Research Summer Research Programme interns gain a unique insight into life as a Quantitative Researcher at a leading quantitative finance research firm.
You will be given a meaningful and challenging research project that demands the application of innovative yet pragmatic mathematical and computational analysis.
Using rigorous scientific methodology, robust statistical analysis and pattern recognition, you will extract meaningful predictive signals from financial time-series and use these to predict future dynamics.
Your project will give you the opportunity to use a wide range of techniques in areas such as mathematical modelling, deep learning, optimisation and machine learning in a practical and challenging context. Additional work may involve the implementation of back-testing frameworks to ensure signal robustness or the creation of a pipeline which constructs and simulates the performance of a portfolio derived from various input signals.
Throughout the internship, you will collaborate closely with a Quantitative Researcher who will mentor you as you complete your independent project. You will receive structured feedback and reviews to help you to improve and develop, culminating in a final presentation of your research ideas to senior management.
Taking part in G-Research's Summer Internship Programme will give you an in-depth insight into our academic approach to quantitative finance. You will also have the opportunity to explore London and get to know your fellow interns and colleagues through a full itinerary of social events.
Top performers on the internship will be considered for full-time opportunities on completion of their studies.
Who are we looking for?
The ideal candidate will have the following skills and experience:
• Strong mathematical background
• Intermediate level of programming in at least one object-oriented language, ideally Python or C#
• Interest in applying data science, machine learning and optimisation techniques to real-world problems
• Be in the final or penultimate year of a Masters or PhD in a highly technical or quantitative subject such as Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Engineering or Computer Science, with a PhD preferred
• Active GitHub or Kaggle profiles are desirable but not essential
• Previous experience in finance is not required, but an interest in finance and a willingness to learn are essential
Why should you apply?
• Highly competitive compensation plus accommodation
• G-Research community with weekly intern activities
• Lunch provided (via Just Eat for Business) and dedicated barista bar
• 30 days’ annual leave pro-rated
• Informal dress code and excellent work/life balance
• Central London office close to 5 stations and 6 tube lines
